meta.session_title: Day 1 - Introduction to Java & Language Fundamentals

front.content: What is the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM?

back.content:
JVM (Java Virtual Machine): Executes compiled bytecode. Platform-specific but makes Java platform-independent.

JRE (Java Runtime Environment): JVM + standard class libraries needed to RUN Java programs. End-users need JRE.

JDK (Java Development Kit): JRE + development tools (compiler javac, debugger, jar, javadoc). Developers need JDK.

Memory trick: JDK ⊃ JRE ⊃ JVM

front.content: What are the 8 primitive data types in Java and their sizes?

back.content:
byte    → 1 byte  → -128 to 127
short   → 2 bytes → -32,768 to 32,767
int     → 4 bytes → ~-2.1B to 2.1B
long    → 8 bytes → ~-9.2 quintillion to 9.2 quintillion
float   → 4 bytes → ~7 decimal digits precision
double  → 8 bytes → ~15 decimal digits precision
char    → 2 bytes → 0 to 65,535 (Unicode)
boolean → 1 bit   → true or false

front.content: What is integer overflow? What happens when you exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE?

back.content:
Integer overflow occurs when an arithmetic operation produces a value outside the range of the data type.

Java does NOT throw an exception — it wraps around silently:

Integer.MAX_VALUE = 2,147,483,647
Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1 = -2,147,483,648 (Integer.MIN_VALUE)

This is a silent bug! Use 'long' or BigInteger for large numbers.
Always validate boundaries in production code.

Output:
2
1
2.5

Explanation:
• x / y = 5 / 2 = 2 (integer division — truncates decimal)
• x % y = 5 % 2 = 1 (remainder/modulo operator)
• (double) x / y = 2.5 (cast x to double first, then divide)

Key: Integer division truncates toward zero, never rounds!

front.content: What is the difference between == and .equals() for Strings in Java?
Explain short-circuit evaluation in Java's && and || operators.

int i = 5;
System.out.println(i++);  // Line A
System.out.println(++i);  // Line B
System.out.println(i);    // Line C

back.content:
Output:
5   (Line A: post-increment — use THEN increment: prints 5, i becomes 6)
7   (Line B: pre-increment — increment THEN use: i becomes 7, prints 7)
7   (Line C: i is 7)

Rule:
• i++ → Returns current value, THEN increments
• ++i → Increments FIRST, THEN returns new value

back.content:
arr.length → 5  (note: no parentheses — it's a field, not a method)

arr[arr.length - 1] → 50 (last element; index is 0-based)

arr[5] → throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at runtime
  (valid indices are 0 to arr.length-1, i.e., 0-4)

Key points:
• Arrays in Java are 0-indexed
• arr.length gives total capacity
• Accessing out-of-bounds is a RUNTIME exception (not compile-time)

front.content: What is platform independence in Java? How does bytecode enable it?

back.content:
Java's motto: 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' (WORA)

How it works:
1. Java source (.java) is compiled by javac → bytecode (.class)
2. Bytecode is NOT machine code — it's JVM instructions
3. Each OS has its own JVM implementation
4. The JVM on that OS interprets/JIT-compiles bytecode to native machine code

Benefit: The SAME .class file runs on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android...
  as long as a JVM is installed for that platform.

Contrast: C/C++ compiles to platform-specific machine code — must recompile for each OS.

front.content: What is an enhanced for loop (for-each)? When should you use it vs a traditional for loop?

back.content:
Enhanced for (for-each) syntax:
for (ElementType element : collection) { ... }

Example:
int[] nums = {1, 2, 3};
for (int n : nums) System.out.println(n);

Use for-each when:
✅ You need to read every element in order
✅ You don't need the index
✅ You don't need to modify the array

Use traditional for when:
❌ You need the index
❌ You iterate backwards or skip elements
❌ You need to modify the array
❌ You need to stop early based on index

front.content: What is implicit (widening) vs explicit (narrowing) type casting in Java?

back.content:
Widening (implicit) — done automatically by compiler:
byte → short → int → long → float → double

int i = 100;
long l = i;   // automatic, no data loss

Narrowing (explicit) — must cast manually, may lose data:
double d = 9.99;
int i = (int) d;  // i = 9 (decimal truncated!)

long bigNum = 300L;
byte b = (byte) bigNum;  // b = 44 (wraps around!)

Rule: Narrowing can LOSE data. Always be intentional.
Common mistake: assuming (int)3.9 rounds to 4 — it doesn't, it's 3.

front.content: What are varargs in Java? Give syntax and a practical example.

back.content:
Output:

Key Arrays class methods:
• Arrays.sort(arr)           → sorts in ascending order (modifies original)
• Arrays.toString(arr)       → returns "[1, 2, 5, 8, 9]" for printing
• Arrays.binarySearch(arr,8) → returns index (ONLY on sorted array)
• Arrays.copyOf(arr, 3)      → new array [1, 2, 5]
• Arrays.fill(arr, 0)        → sets all elements to 0
• Arrays.equals(a, b)        → true if same length and elements

What are Java naming conventions? Give examples for each.

back.content:
Classes:    PascalCase     → BankAccount, CustomerService, ArrayList
Interfaces: PascalCase     → Serializable, Runnable, Comparable
Methods:    camelCase      → calculateInterest(), getUserName()
Variables:  camelCase      → accountBalance, firstName, isActive
Constants:  UPPER_SNAKE    → MAX_BALANCE, PI, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT
Packages:   lowercase      → com.mycompany.banking.service

Boolean naming:
• Use is/has/can prefix → isValid(), hasAccount(), canWithdraw()

These are CONVENTIONS not rules — code compiles without them.
But violating them is a code smell and fails code reviews!

front.content: What does 'strongly typed' mean in Java? What are the benefits?

back.content:
Strongly typed: Every variable MUST have a declared type, and type rules are strictly enforced at compile-time.

Examples:
int count = 'A';   // OK — char 'A' (65) widens to int
int x = "hello"; // COMPILE ERROR — String can't be int
bool flag = 1;    // COMPILE ERROR — no implicit int-to-bool

Benefits:
✅ Catches type mismatches at compile-time (not runtime)
✅ Better IDE support (autocomplete, refactoring)
✅ Self-documenting code — type communicates intent
✅ Prevents entire classes of runtime bugs

Contrast: Python/JavaScript are dynamically typed — type errors found at runtime.
